question: Ivermectin is indicated in all of the following except:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Ivermectin is an antiparasitic medication" -> "effective against certain parasitic infections" -> "indicated for Onchocerciasis" -> "indicated for Filariasis" -> "not indicated for Malaria" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Ivermectin treats various parasitic infections" -> "approved for use in Onchocerciasis" -> "approved for use in Filariasis" -> "not effective against Plasmodium species" -> "Malaria is caused by Plasmodium" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Ivermectin is used for specific parasitic diseases" -> "effective for Ascaris" -> "effective for Onchocerciasis" -> "effective for Filariasis" -> "ineffective for Malaria" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Ivermectin is indicated for certain infections" -> "indicated for Onchocerciasis" -> "indicated for Filariasis" -> "not indicated for Malaria" -> "Malaria requires different treatment" -> 92%
analysis: Ivermectin is an antiparasitic medication that is primarily indicated for certain parasitic infections. It is well-established that Ivermectin is effective against Onchocerciasis (option opd) and Filariasis (option opb), both of which are caused by parasitic worms. While Ivermectin may have some activity against Ascaris (option opa), it is not the first-line treatment; other anthelmintics like albendazole or mebendazole are preferred. Most importantly, Ivermectin is not indicated for Malaria (option opc), which is caused by Plasmodium species and requires specific antimalarial treatments. Therefore, the only option that Ivermectin is not indicated for is Malaria. This aligns with the consensus in pharmacology regarding the use of Ivermectin. Thus, the correct answer is option opc.
